To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the acquisition of knowledge about complex probabilistic sequences is characterized by an increasing ability to generate and to recognize the sequence, and that this increase in generation performance is accompanied by a decrease in reaction times.
reaction times and generation performance are correlated and that the correlation is higher after than before training.

(i) reaction time and generation data are strongly correlated; (ii) this correlation increases with learning; and (iii) generation data can be analyzed using hidden Markov models to characterize knowledge in terms of grammar.

the question of whether and how subjects can express knowledge about probabilistic sequences and how this knowledge can be characterized in a more formal way.
